sense: cautiously, so as not to fall, break or hurt

evidence: Plaut. Trin. 2.2.46: cautē et cōgitātē rem tractāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From cautus, wary (caveō, beware): with care against danger or mistakes. In Cicero also “with proper security”, of a thing done with guarantees (Lewis & Short). To warn someone, say cavē nē … (see careful, don’t fall).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.14.7: pedetemptim et gradātim (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “feeling one’s way with the feet”: slowly, a step at a time, and so “cautiously, by degrees” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: to handle the matter carefully and thoughtfully

phrases.latin: In viā pergit cautē (prōvidē), nē impingat aut aberret.
phrases.english: She goes along the road carefully, so as not to stumble or lose her way.
Carry the cup carefully; it’s glass.
